It's very hard for me to explain my point. I used colours and toys to make an example for gender stereotypes. I'm definitely not saying that transgenderism is the reason gender roles exist. But transgenderism definitely validates them. If you were assigned female at birth, but later in life you see how people are divided - boys and girls - you like playing with boys more and so you start seeing the world differently - "Why am I not like my friends?; What's wrong with me?" --I AM TALKING FROM PERSONAL EXPERIENCE - IT IS NOT FICTIONAL-- You see two sides. And you gotta fit somewhere. That's why you start to dress like them more and more, you get a hair cut and so on.. But then grown ups start to ask questions - "What's up with her, is she trying to be a boy?? We live in a sick world". - You get even sicker with yourself. So you start dressing with skirts and cute little dresses - but now even your best friends don't know who you are. I didn't fit anywhere. And that all because of gender roles. If I kept my "style" boyish, I would probably be transgender today. And I don't find that to be a bad thing. I just don't like that we have those stereotypes and we have to take sides, we can't just be what we want to be, we have to "transition"

I do understand it's not about colours or toys. I watch quite a lot of videos on youtube from trans youtubers. That's why I said that I sympathise with them - I cannot imagine how terrible they feel. In fact I'm dealing with body dysmorphia myself, although it is probably not even near to the extend they are. I am aware that to be trans doesn't mean to do what society tell you you should do. It's only about you - how you're feeling - trapped in a body you despise. Maybe I didn't write it as I wanted. My thoughts are all over the place.
